headline: Fantasy football: Ranking the best, worst landing spots for Jonathan Taylor
description: It may be just a matter of time before Taylor is dealt, so Michael F. Florio ranks his potential destinations.
story: There are two factors that go into determining the best and worst fantasy football landing spots for Jonathan Taylor . The first is what is best for Taylor. I fully believe he is an elite talent and will succeed anywhere. And any team trading for him has to be in a better situation than the Indianapolis Colts , who have traded their top offensive lineman. They have also had poor quarterback play and often trail, which means a negative game script for the running game. However, Taylor is also going to crater the fantasy value of the running backs on whichever team he is dealt to. That should be considered as well. Best Jonathan Taylor landing spots 1. Minnesota Vikings : I would expect any team that acquires Taylor to use him plenty, but the Vikings and their style of play make a lot of sense. They have run the ball at the sixth-highest rate this season. They want to establish the run and trust their defense. Minnesota has created the third-most yards before contact on RB carries, so its offensive line is creating running lanes for the backs. This is a situation where Taylor would get to come in and become the immediate focal point on a team very much in the hunt. It could also help open things up in the passing game, which Justin Jefferson managers would enjoy. Lastly, neither of the Vikings' current running backs is a great fantasy option. Since Jordan Mason returned, neither he nor Aaron Jones Sr . has scored seven fantasy points in a game. 2. Seattle Seahawks : This would ruin the fantasy values of Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet , but neither has provided much anyway. The Seahawks have struggled to create consistent running lanes, as evidenced by their 0.6 yards before contact per carry (NFL average: 0.9); however, we should see improvements there with recent acquisition Quenton Nelson on the offensive line. This is the rare instance where Taylor would not be the focal point of opposing defenses, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on the perimeter. 3. Cincinnati Bengals : This would hurt in fantasy as it would take Chase Brown out as a weekly option. However, the Bengals' offense would be the NFL version of the "Monstars" with Taylor added. Good luck stacking the box and leaving Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase to run wild in the secondary. 4. Washington Commanders : The Commanders are creating running lanes, but their backs have struggled to consistently produce. Taylor would immediately change that, on a team that has a ton of touches up for grabs. Taylor getting to run the option with Jayden Daniels should make fantasy managers of either player salivate. We have yet to see Daniels paired with a dominant running back. 5. New England Patriots : The Patriots' backs might produce at times for fantasy, but they have struggled all season. Both Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson have averaged under 4 yards per carry. In fact, both have negative rush EPAs on the season. Taylor would come in, see the bulk of work, and give New England potentially three elite offensive players when A.J. Brown returns. Worst Jonathan Taylor landing spots 1. Denver Broncos : My answer for the worst fantasy landing spot for Taylor might surprise some. The Broncos are struggling on the ground despite a strong offensive line. They rank just above league average in yards before contact, and their current backs have picked up yards after contact at the lowest rate in the NFL and explosive runs at the fifth-lowest rate. Taylor would elevate this, but my biggest concern is usage. Under Sean Payton, the Broncos have been more of a "sum of their parts" offense. Perhaps acquiring Taylor would change that, but people said the same thing when the team acquired Jaylen Waddle . Taylor would obviously see the most touches for Denver, but would we see the other backs mixed in and eating into his workload? Fantasy managers have long been burned by Payton's unpredictable shenanigans. Plus, this would wreck the fantasy value of Jonah Coleman , who has the potential to be a breakout star this season. Coleman ranks third among running backs in explosive run rate and has shown to be the most effective Broncos RB in the running and passing games. He has league-winning upside if he gets to remain as the lead back. 2. Green Bay Packers : The Packers make sense given Josh Jacobs ' off-the-field situation; however, they have been vocal that they expect him to remain with the team. Green Bay is tied for the second-fewest yards before contact per carry (0.4). Its offensive line has struggled to create running lanes all season. Plus, the Packers have found their most success since Jordan Love began airing the ball out. Between the offensive line struggles and Jacobs' presence, this would not be a great landing spot. 3. New York Giants : Taylor would produce anywhere, but to varying degrees. The Giants have created 0.5 rushing yards before contact per carry, which is tied for the fourth lowest in the NFL. I'd expect him to see a heavy dose of stacked boxes here,

headline: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy, claims he owes over $3.45M in debts
description: Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy in federal court, claiming he has more than $3.45 million in debts.
story: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy in federal court Wednesday, claiming he has more than $3.45 million in debts, according to federal court records. Rice, who filed in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court, claimed more than $2.1 million of his debts are tied to varying plaintiffs suing him in civil litigations that have either been settled or are awaiting trial. Rice, 26, has been sued by multiple individuals for his role in a high-speed multicar crash in Dallas in 2024 and an ex-girlfriend alleging he repeatedly assaulted her from 2023 to 2025. In the filing, Rice claimed to have $677,054 in personal assets, including $421,825 in "deferred compensation." The filing claims Rice has $13,640 in his checking accounts. He claims to rent a residence and that he does not own any property. Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which is for "individuals who have financial difficulty preventing them from paying their debts and who are willing to allow their non-exempt property to be used to pay their creditors," according to the bankruptcy filing. Rice claimed $39,241 of his personal assets to be nonexempt. The documents claim Rice's largest creditor is still owed $979,837 as part of a 2025 civil settlement related to the crash. Rice is disputing potential debts in some of the civil trials, including a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit. According to the documents, Rice used his Super Bowl LVIII ring, which he valued at $160,000, as collateral with Thomas McMurray, his attorney in the pending civil litigations. Rice's bankruptcy attorney, David Shuster, and the Chiefs had no comment about the bankruptcy filing. McMurray did not immediately respond to messages left by ESPN seeking comment. Rice is in the final year of his rookie contract with the Chiefs and is expected to make $1,560,711 in base salary in 2026. He has played in five games this season, with 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Jonathan Taylor 'can't avoid' trade speculation as Colts go through talks
description: Running back Jonathan Taylor, who is the subject of talks between the Colts and multiple teams ahead of the NFL trade deadline, said he's ready for some finality after weeks of speculation about his future.
story: INDIANAPOLIS -- As the rest of the NFL awaits the outcome of the Jonathan Taylor trade talks, the Indianapolis Colts star running back says he is just as anxious for a conclusion as everyone else. Taylor, who is the subject of talks between the Colts and multiple teams ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, said he is ready for some finality after weeks of speculation about his future. "No one wants uncertainty," Taylor said Thursday, adding, "Until the past couple weeks, it's kind of been the same thing. But it won't be until Tuesday at [4 p.m.] where you'll know exactly what's going on, you'll know exactly what the verdict is." The Colts (2-6) have been headed for an apparent reboot in recent weeks, beginning with the firing of general manager Chris Ballard last month and the trades of guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner a week later. Taylor, wide receiver Josh Downs and others have become trade targets of other teams, as the Colts continue to mull offers with the goal of stockpiling draft picks. As a result, Taylor's future has become one of the biggest stories in the NFL in recent weeks. The Colts' career rushing touchdown leader and second-leading rusher behind Edgerrin James, Taylor, 27, is coveted by teams trying to make a playoff run. "You can't avoid it," Taylor said. "Internet, all of that stuff. You can't avoid it. But it's more about trying to block that out. Let's say you're getting online. Whatever you're getting online to do, go get it done. And whether you have some type of marketing obligation, get it done, and then you're off of it. But you're not going to avoid it, not until it's all over." For now, Taylor is focused on Sunday's home game against the Dallas Cowboys . Indianapolis suffered an embarrassing 42-7 loss at Jacksonville last week, with Taylor held to 23 rushing yards on eight carries. He sat out the fourth quarter because of the huge deficit in the game. Coach Shane Steichen said Taylor will play against the Cowboys despite the trade talks, and Taylor confirmed his intent to play. Sunday's game could be Taylor's last as a member of the Colts, but he said he will focus on winning, not his personal situation. "You don't want external factors creeping in and trying to alter your play," he said.
